title: OpenFeature eval context must use concrete namespace, never wildcard '*'
answers: Why do flag evaluations fail with a namespace mismatch for cluster-wide/service tokens?
OpenFeature targeting key is '*' and gets rejected downstream
How is the namespace chosen for OpenFeature evaluation context?
Feature flag requests rejected due to namespace mismatch when using wildcard identity
body:
Symptom: requests authenticated with a wildcard identity namespace (e.g. cluster-wide service token) get their OpenFeature flag evaluations rejected downstream as a namespace mismatch.
Root cause: pkg/services/contexthandler/contexthandler.go:setRequestContext used id.Namespace directly to build the OpenFeature evaluation context whenever id != nil, even if that namespace was empty or the wildcard '*', which doesn't match the caller's concrete auth namespace.
Fix pattern: when deriving a namespace/targeting-key value from an identity for use in a downstream system, explicitly fall back to a concrete value (stack namespace or 'default') whenever the identity's namespace is empty or a wildcard sentinel ('*') — don't propagate wildcard/sentinel values into contexts that require exact matching.
Constraints: applies to any code building openfeature.NewEvaluationContext or similar targeting contexts from identity.Namespace; does not apply to authz checks where '*' is a valid intentional wildcard match.
applies: pkg/services/contexthandler when building OpenFeature evaluation context from request identity

search: When building an OpenFeature evaluation context in pkg/services/contexthandler/contexthandler.go:setRequestContext, replace wildcard '*' or empty identity.Namespace with a concrete fallback (stack namespace or 'default') rather than propagating the sentinel. Wildcard namespaces in downstream flag evaluations cause namespace-mismatch rejections; this constraint does not apply to authorization checks where '*' is a valid wildcard. Necessary for any code deriving a targeting-key from identity.Namespace for openfeature.NewEvaluationContext or similar exact-match targeting systems.
